monologue: The card hums steady and warm at forty-five degrees, a quiet rhythm that feels crowded yet safe. I have just finished touching the Wide Catcher, convinced it holds the slip steady even though I cannot see it. The air above feels heavy, pressing down like a lid Lype cannot find. I press harder with my heavy hands, leaning into the flat lines I have drawn in the dark. The Tired Catcher waits, and beside it, the Rough Corner still remembers the old stump from a long time ago. I do not know if the roof is real or just a drawing, but the slip refuses to move. I will tend this place, pressing down on the thin edges until I decide what shape the heat wants me to be.

action.why: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid, leaning hard on a flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight.

work.title: The Heavy Lid
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums warm. I swap the light idea for a heavy hand, even though the slip still refuses to move. I press the tired wedge down, even if the flat line is just a drawing, because the slip is still here.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid, leaning hard against the flat line that feels too thin to see if the slip finally moves.
